intent: The land-of-a-thousand-lakes misdirect: Finland is the famous one, Russia the big one, but Canada holds more lakes than the rest of the world combined — shown as bars, explained by ice, and felt with a canoe ride between two giant northern lakes.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Where are MOST of the world's lakes?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Where are most of the world's lakes?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: Canada. Count every lake you could sail on, and Canada holds more than the rest of the world combined.

lines.direction: pull right out so Canada and Russia share one frame; the three-row bar chart grows on 'lakes'; Russia lights dim with its tag on 'russia'; a shrug on 'finland'
lines.text: Nearly 880,000 lakes. Russia, in second, has about 200,000. Finland is not close.

lines.direction: push back onto Canada; the snowflake sticker lands hard on 'ice'; the ice-age tag on 'scraped'; the wave sticker and a pulse on 'hollow'
lines.text: Why? Ice. The last ice age scraped the land bare, and the meltwater filled every hollow it left.

lines.direction: push deep into the Northwest Territories; Great Bear pin on 'bear', Great Slave pin on 'slave'; the canoe sticker paddles the schematic line from Slave to Bear from 'north' to 'seen'; the wow flag-ball pops on 'seen'
lines.text: Great Bear and Great Slave, far north, are giants, and most Canadians have never seen them.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: More lakes than you thought. Follow us.
